title: Director of Marketing

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: This role owns Roland DGA's market positioning, customer education, and go-to-market messaging—critical for introducing Tedlar as part of Roland's recommended media stack. Given Roland's substantial trade show presence (PRINTING United 2024/2025, ISA 2024, Impressions 2026) and live vehicle wrap demonstrations, the marketing team actively shapes customer perceptions about durability and quality. They would care about: (1) Elevating Roland's brand positioning from '3-4 years outdoor durability' to '12-20+ years with Tedlar protection'—a transformative marketing message that repositions Roland as the premium choice for long-term outdoor applications, (2) Creating co-marketing content, case studies, and ROI calculators that demonstrate Tedlar's graffiti resistance, UV protection, and TCO benefits to Roland's target buyers (sign shops, wrap installers, architectural graphics companies), (3) Differentiating Roland's TrueVIS and VersaCAMM product lines in crowded trade show environments where competitors like Mimaki and HP Latex compete on similar specs, and (4) Supporting customer retention and referral programs by delivering measurably superior long-term results that generate testimonials and reduce churn. Their KPIs around brand awareness, lead generation quality, and customer satisfaction scores would improve significantly with Tedlar as a documented performance advantage in marketing campaigns and product launch materials for new printer series.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As Director of Marketing, [Name] owns Roland DGA's brand positioning, customer messaging, trade show strategy, and educational content for their wide-format printer portfolio (TrueVIS, VersaCAMM, VersaOBJECT lines). This role shapes how Roland's 3M MCS and Avery Dennison ICS certified products are positioned to sign manufacturers, vehicle wrap installers, and large-format print shops across North and South America. They likely report to a VP or Chief Marketing Officer and collaborate closely with Product Management and Sales leadership. While they don't directly control procurement decisions, they influence go-to-market strategy, partnership messaging, and customer education materials that drive adoption of recommended media solutions. Their authority extends to co-marketing partnerships, trade show messaging, case study development, and digital content strategy—all critical for introducing Tedlar as part of Roland's durability narrative.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given Roland's focus on outdoor signage, vehicle wraps, and durable graphics, three Tedlar use cases would directly support [Name]'s marketing objectives: (1) Vehicle Wraps & Fleet Graphics—Tedlar's graffiti resistance and UV protection would enable Roland to market vehicle wrap solutions that maintain appearance for 12-20 years vs. the current 3-4 year standard, creating a premium positioning opportunity for Roland's TrueVIS line against Mimaki and HP Latex competitors; (2) Outdoor Signs & Graphics—Tedlar eliminates the yellowing, fading, and cracking issues that generate customer complaints and warranty claims, allowing [Name] to develop marketing campaigns emphasizing 'install once, forget about it for decades' TCO benefits for Roland's sign shop customers; (3) Architectural Graphics & Building Wraps—Tedlar's weather resistance (-70°F to 230°F) and mold/mildew resistance would differentiate Roland's UV flatbed solutions (EU-1000MF) for exterior architectural applications where long-term performance justifies premium pricing. Each use case provides concrete marketing proof points that [Name] can leverage in trade show demonstrations, customer testimonials, and competitive positioning materials.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: As Director of Marketing, [Name] is likely measured on: brand differentiation metrics (how Roland stands out vs. Mimaki, HP, Epson in customer perception studies), lead generation quality and volume (particularly from high-value trade shows like PRINTING United and ISA Sign Expo where Roland invests heavily), customer education engagement (webinar attendance, content downloads, case study views), and indirectly on customer retention and satisfaction scores that reflect product positioning accuracy. Tedlar directly addresses [Name]'s core pain points: (1) Competitive differentiation—Roland currently competes on similar 3-4 year outdoor durability specs as competitors; Tedlar enables a '12-20+ year protection' message that no competitor can match without adopting Tedlar themselves; (2) Trade show ROI—with confirmed booth presence at PRINTING United 2025 (Orlando) and Impressions Expo 2026, [Name] needs compelling demonstrations that convert booth visitors into qualified leads; live demos showing Tedlar's graffiti resistance (spray paint wiping off) would create memorable moments; (3) Customer complaint reduction—marketing teams inherit blame when product reality doesn't match promises; Tedlar eliminates the gap between '3-4 year outdoor durability' claims and actual field performance, protecting Roland's brand reputation; (4) Premium positioning—[Name] can reframe Roland's value proposition from 'reliable printer' to 'total solution for permanent outdoor graphics,' supporting higher price points and improved gross margins that make marketing ROI calculations more favorable.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Three timing factors make NOW an optimal engagement moment: (1) Roland DGA is confirmed exhibiting at PRINTING United Expo 2025 in Orlando (September) and Impressions Expo 2026—[Name]'s team is actively planning booth messaging, demos, and differentiation strategies for these high-investment events where Tedlar could serve as a centerpiece demonstration (e.g., side-by-side durability tests, graffiti resistance live demo); (2) Roland launched the TY-300 DTF printer in early 2026 and the EU-1000MF UV flatbed recently, indicating active product launch cycles where [Name] is developing launch marketing materials and positioning strategies—Tedlar could be integrated into new product messaging as a recommended overlaminate for outdoor applications; (3) Roland's parent company (Roland DG Japan) reported $373.8M revenue in 2023, suggesting North American growth targets for Roland DGA's $119.4M business—[Name] is likely under pressure to find differentiation strategies that drive market share gains in the competitive wide-format printer market, making Tedlar a timely strategic marketing asset. Additionally, vehicle wrap demonstrations (Tesla Cybertruck at PRINTING United 2024, NASCAR at ISA 2024) show Roland's marketing team is comfortable with bold, visual demonstrations—Tedlar's graffiti resistance and UV protection lend themselves to similarly impactful trade show activations.

personalization_hooks.hook: Roland's current TrueVIS printers are certified for 3-4 years outdoor durability with TR2 eco-solvent inks, but vehicle wrap and outdoor signage customers increasingly demand longer-lasting solutions to reduce replacement costs and downtime
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar as the missing piece that transforms Roland's messaging from '3-4 years certified' to '12-20+ years proven protection'—a 4-5x improvement that would redefine Roland's competitive positioning in marketing materials, trade show messaging, and customer education content without requiring any changes to Roland's printer hardware or inks

personalization_hooks.hook: Roland DGA is exhibiting at PRINTING United Expo 2025 (Orlando) and has a history of impactful live demonstrations like the Tesla Cybertruck wrap at PRINTING United 2024 and NASCAR wrap at ISA 2024
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Propose a co-marketing trade show demonstration concept: a side-by-side durability test booth showing Roland-printed graphics with standard laminate vs. Tedlar overlaminate after accelerated weathering, plus a live graffiti resistance demo where booth visitors spray paint a Tedlar-protected Roland print and watch it wipe clean—creating a memorable, shareable moment that drives booth traffic and lead generation

personalization_hooks.hook: Roland competes directly with Mimaki, HP Latex, and Epson in the wide-format printer market, and the Director of Marketing needs differentiation angles that justify premium positioning for Roland's TrueVIS and VersaCAMM product lines
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame Tedlar as a strategic marketing asset that enables Roland to own the 'permanent outdoor graphics' category—while competitors focus on printer specs and ink chemistry, Roland can market complete solutions (printer + ink + Tedlar overlaminate) with documented 12-20+ year field performance, creating a unique value proposition that supports higher ASPs and improved customer lifetime value that [Name] can use in competitive battle cards and sales enablement materials

recommended_approach: Lead with the trade show opportunity angle—reference Roland's upcoming PRINTING United 2025 presence and history of impactful demonstrations, then position Tedlar as a co-marketing asset that would create a memorable booth experience and differentiate Roland's messaging from competitors. Follow with the competitive positioning benefit (3-4 years to 12-20+ years transformation) as a strategic marketing narrative that [Name] can deploy across campaigns, case studies, and product launch materials. Emphasize Tedlar as a marketing enabler rather than a technical material spec, focusing on how it solves [Name]'s brand differentiation and lead generation challenges.
